spans.s:
हेति, इस्, m. f. a weapon, missile; stroke, wound,
injury, (Sāy. = हिंसा, Ṛg-veda

); a ray
of the sun; light, splendor; flame; (इस्), m., N. of
the first Rākṣasa king (father of Vidyut-keśa; repre-
sented as residing in the Sun's chariot in the month
of Caitra or Madhu).
—हेति-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, pos-
sessed of weapons, armed with missiles (Ved.);
illuminated by the sun.
हेतिक = हेति (at the end of a comp., cf. शक्ति-ह्˚).

. fr. rt.
1. हि), impulse, motive; cause, reason, object, pur-
pose (e. g. अनेन हेतुना, for this reason; मृत्यु-
हेतवे, in order to kill; हेतुर् अलौकिकः, a super-
natural cause); a logical reason, the reason for an
inference (constituting the second Avayava or mem-
ber of the five-membered Nyāya syllogism, e. g.
1. ‘this hill is fiery,’ 2. ‘because it smokes;’ see न्य्-
आय, p. 519; 2. प्रति-ज्ञा, p. 613); any logical deduc-
tion or argument, proof; reasoning, logic (in general);
excuse, sophistry; means, instrument; law, condition;
source, origin; a particular figure of speech, (in the
drama) a brief speech giving a reason; (हेतुना or
हेतौ or हेतोस्), ind. by reason of, because of, on
account of, for the sake of, (generally after a gen. or
at the end of a comp., e. g. मम हेतोः or मद्-
धेतोः, on account of me.)
—हेतु-ता, f. or हेतु-
त्व, अम्, n. the state of being a हेतु or cause,
causation, cause, causativeness, the abstract existence
of cause or motive.
—हेतु-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having
a reason or cause, proceeding from a cause (as any
effect); having the Hetu (or second Avayava of a
syllogism); accompanied by arguments; controverted
by arguments.
—हेतु-वाद, अस्, m. a statement of
[]
reasons or argument, assigning a cause, disputation.
—हेतु-शास्त्र, अम्, n. a rationalistic book, (Manu

); any heretical or sceptical work calling in
question the authority of Śruti.
—हेतु-शास्त्राश्रय
(˚र-आश्˚), अस्, m. reliance on rationalistic treatises.
—हेतु-श्लिष्ट, (in rhetoric) combination of cause,
a method of comparing two objects by using epithets
common to both so as to describe similar results in
each produced by similar causes.
—हेतु-हेतुमद्-
भाव, अस्, m. the relation subsisting between cause
and effect.
—हेतूपन्यास (˚तु-उप्˚), अस्, m. the
assignment of reasons or motives, statement of an
argument.
—हेत्व्-अपदेश, the adducing or men-
tioning of the reason (or second member of the
syllogism in logic).
—हेत्व्-आभास, अस्, m. (in logic)
a mere appearance of a reason, fallacious semblance
of an argument, fallacious middle term, fallacy (said
to be of five kinds, viz. व्य्-अभिचार or स-व्य-
भिचार, वि-रुद्ध, अ-सिद्ध, सत्-प्रतिपक्ष,
बाध or बाधित); the bringing forward or stating
of a Hetu (or second member of a syllogism), the
assignment of a reason which can be shown to be
incorrect.

हेतुक, अस्, m. a cause, active cause, instrument
(= हेतु); a logician; (अस्, आ, अम्), causal, instru-
mental, belonging to a motive or cause; causing,
producing (at the end of comps., e. g. विषाद-ह्˚,
causing dejection); N. of a poet.

हेतृ, ता, त्री, तृ, Ved. urging on, inciting; (ता),
m. an inciter.
